On 24 May 2001 16:28:06 -0700, David Cherryholmes wrote:

>However, this is for the GF, and she likes 'em straight forward
>and disposable. We're working on her......

I have a weenie fortitude deck. It's simple and effective and it's
the only deck my girlfriend is prepared to play too. I'll show you
mine if you show me yours. Drop me an email - let the canaille find
out the hard way.

Sabbat War contained some weenie-hosers but I have the impression that
they've not had much impression on the metagame. I'd expect Final
Nights to make them more popular again. Old, expensive vampires
already have ToGP and Rush to worry about. If the Assamites become
effective at making hits and the Followers of Set become effective at
stealing minions then this would swing the metagame even more
decisively against them.

The basic problem is that the game's mechanics are stacked so firmly
against the older vampires. What's the point of buying a 10-cap with
6 different disciplines when you can't feasibly use more than a couple
of them? They have titles but it's trivial for the weenie to acquire
those too. All the old vampires have going for them is the 5th
Trad/Minion Tap pool engine but that's sick and wrong too.

Not that the rest of WoD isn't silly too. The Kindred show just had
some Brujah/Ventrue feuding in which a Ventrue Archon had a fit of
remorse and just himself be blown away. And Julian's as soppy as ever
- would rather suffer Final Death than take blood from his new
girlfriend. Maybe this Prince is really a weenie too.

Meanwhile, in the computer game, Christof has just reached London
where he is having to slaughter his way through the Society of
Leopold. They deserve it for those awful fake Cockney accents but
you'd expect the occasional pang of remorse from our noble hero in
this case. Not a bit of it - his humanity score is as high as ever.
He's newly embraced, you see and that makes him another uber-weenie.

We were playing Shadowfist at the club last night - now that's a game
in which mooks are cannon-fodder and royalty kicks butt. But my eye
kept straying to the role-players where one chap had brought his
attractive goth girlfriend. It would take more than a weenie to
impress her, I fancy ...

Andrew

Messages.Author: David Cherryholmes
Messages.Body:
Tried to reply via email, but the message got bounced back due
to the domain being unresolveable. Hmmm.... mail's been
getting funky around here lately (sorry about the initial
double post... went to Google for the second one since the first one
wasn't showing on my end).

In any case, here's the reply:

I'm at work and I don't have the deck archived here, but I'll happily
give you the gist of it:

Crypt: the twelve smallest guys with fortitude (got 'em all)

Master: 7 Fortitudes (having FOR is important for this one)
4 Tributes (see below)
3 Effective Managements (staple weenie-deck master)

Library: (all numbers are approximate)

12 Rapid Healing
8 Restoration
8 Undead Persistance
8 Traps
8 Force of Will
6 Freak Drives
6 Day Operations
4 Dawn Operations
4 Amaranth

I'm sure you're familiar with the FoW schtick, so you know the challenge
is always how to "get sideways" without bleeding. I've done it a few
different ways in the past (rushes, equips, et al.). This time around,
I'm thinking do a few bleeds for one to either get into trapped combat to
get light enough to hunt or kill time until the Tribute shows up. Then
*wham*, nice pool gain and all your guys are hunt-legit.

The rest is pretty standard, so I won't waste time explaining the obvious
:) Weenie-hood handles the critical point of successfully rapid-healing
out of torpor without getting blocked (overwhelm their blocking ability or
revel in you minions disposable-ness if they are truly hard-core about
keeping you there). Having another minion do the rescue also takes care
of the doom scenario of minions at full blood cap as another, lesser,
alternative. I suspect I need to have more, lots more, tributes in there,
but master space is tight. I'll probably cut down on the FOR skill cards
a wee bit, and throw in a couple Parthenons or something.

There ya go!

David Cherryholmes

As an idle note, it is a legal action to hunt while full. The blood
drains off immediately, so you gain nothing, but you may still hunt
even if you are at full capacity. So it's not quite AS difficult to
tap. =)

Consider a copy of Cairo International Airport, Powerbase: Montreal,
The Rack, Fragment of the Book of Nod, and any other "steal-me-please"
Master cards. These make for more useful and productive tap actions,
since if you have it, you get the benefit, and you can always 'waste'
an action going to take it back. =) And Cairo can be a truly
offensive thing if someone leaves blood on an uncontrolled minion -
tap out taking Cairo actions, then everyone bleeds for 3 with Force of
Will.

>alternative. I suspect I need to have more, lots more, tributes in there,
>but master space is tight. I'll probably cut down on the FOR skill cards
>a wee bit, and throw in a couple Parthenons or something.

Definitely a Parthenon (only one). Also consider four or five Rumors
of Gehenna cards - sell the Master phase actions to the guys with the
votes, and unless your predator has vote lock, you're golden. =)

-- Derek

Ran the deck last night. It had evolved away from weenies; once I put
the crack pipe down I realized they just didn't have the capacity to
support the combo. Nudged the crypt up to 6 or so choice vampires of cap
3-5 (the 5's were Camille -- don't own a Raven). Also ditched Undead
Persistance and Trap and went with more of the combo-cards and added some
regular old stealth. Since the crypt was now mostly Gangrel, in go the
Garou's (4! ...rush is this deck's answer to intercept, and it bloats well
enough to pay) and all the juicy Gangrel location Masters.

Turn one Rikki got out, turn two did the Fow-watch me get out of torpor
schtick. Everyone said "cute" and snickered at how little blood was left
after my bleed for 2. Then, after I had four blood dolls out and Eco
Terrorists, and *3* Garou, and was bleeding for 3 multiple times, mostly
unblockable, it wasn't so "cute" anymore. Which is a long-winded way of
saying "it worked." However, most of these guys didn't start playing
until after the change to Fame and hadn't seen FoW-MotSB-RH-FD. Any
deck's chances to rock go way up if no-one thinks you're a threat.

Realizing this is old hat for most of us, but, hey, might be news to
somebody.

David Cherryholmes

Hey... >deep breath< I agree with Andrew S. Davidson... This is the
grounds for which I never really had so much of a problem with Tomb of
Ramses before the new text. Mind you, it still does what it was
supposed to do, bring up larger vamps quickly, but I see the drawback
to 8+ capacity vamps as fully justifying its old text, along with the
fact that newer large caps (Sabbat era forward) tend to have better
discipline sets and more powerful specials. This goes a ways towards
making them stronger, but balanced against the simple equation that
smaller minions give you more actions per turn? Not yet. That's the
real driving force behind MT/5th decks. #1) When pulled off, you get
back your investment in the large vamp. #2) if said vamp gets stomped,
you can get more. The risk factor with large vamps will always be
higher, and the difficulty in getting actions that justify their cost
is difficult, especially when actions that have significant game
impact are often discipline based, rather than capacity based...

Messages.Author: Andrew S. Davidson
Messages.Body:
On Sun, 27 May 2001 21:14:22 GMT, R. David Zopf wrote:

>>We were playing Shadowfist at the club last night - now that's a game
>>in which mooks are cannon-fodder and royalty kicks butt.
>
>... Not that you're ooohhh_biased_ or anything ;-) In truth, SF is a
>fun game, but has a thematic background that draws even less potential
>players than VTES... Good luck to Z-Man keeping it going.

Shadowfist's theme is the most protean of any of the CCG. The time
war backstory is a good excuse to mix and match any of the action
movie tropes. All it's really missing is space opera but it would be
easy to add a Stargate element if one wanted.

The HK movie style is now mainstream - movies and shows like Crouching
Tiger, The Matrix and Dark Angel are big and successful. Buffy has
done great by taking the lighter elements of this style and mixing
them with the tropes of the vampire movie, just as Xena did with
classical myth. Their camp humour and martial arts are very
Shadowfist in tone.

VTES and WoD are stuck in the rut of paranoid, millenial angst which
seems passé now. The shows and movies which typify this don't work so
well, if they ever did - X-Files, Millenium, Forever Knight, Hannibal,
Kindred, Nosferatu.

Of course, the taste of the public can be quite mysterious. I
continue to be amazed at the success of 7th Sea when the last good
pirate movie was Muppet Treasure Island. Is today's youth still
exposed to swashbuckling stuff like Captain Blood and the Crimson
Pirate?

Andrew

walkover - they obviously hadn't got their Final Nights cards yet.

Have taken ship to NYC where the Sabbat Nosferatu seem more of a
challenge. But we're rather puzzled by Club Torrie which seems to
have closed its doors. Doesn't Manhattan have some night life? I'm
getting tired of going to the New Moon instead where the jewish
proprietress keeps hitting on Christof.

Looking forward to the next session as I've been reading the manual on
assault rifles and see now why they might be more useful than shotguns
- area fire sounds good. But Christof has another new toy - he's just
splurged on a rocket launcher and can't wait to try it out on an
ghouled alligator...

Andrew

I asure you. 7th Seas is one of the best systems I've ever played. It serves

Roleplaying (rules are the less important if your description fits)... Well,
i must confess that i'm 26 and ave been playing for 14 years, but in our RPG

Anyway, the movie guionist recycle through themes: Look at the
Sci-fi/Fantasy/Adventure genres. There hasn't been a good set of movies

Messages.Author: James Coupe
Messages.Body:
In message
<664E8E26948481B1.C04E9E99...@lp.airnews.net>,
Andrew S. Davidson <a...@csi.com> writes

>Shadowfist's theme is the most protean of any of the CCG.

Which is a blessing and a curse.

You can try and convince someone to play the bits that appeal to them,
but the other bits just feel "out of place" because it's so alien.

Whereas in, say, Vampire, everything attempts[0] to stay in a certain
theme, so everything feels kind of coherent. The same applies to lots
of other games, each taking a specific genre (roughly) and working with
it. Shadowfist has lots of elements which "grate" if you don't like
that specific theme. (e.g. if you don't like cyborgs)

[0] Of course, things fuck up sometimes.

that's why i like cards such as kiss of ra and speed of thought.
